findings.title: _scrape_listing_urls SSRF guard is a denylist (is_private/loopback/...) without is_global -> accepts CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10
findings.detail: The subscription-scanner listing fetch validates the resolved IP with a DENYLIST: `is_private or is_loopback or is_link_local or is_multicast or is_reserved or is_unspecified` (566-568). This is the exact VR-P15/DP-11 class that invariant I0003 fixed in provider_resolve_impl/_common.py by switching to a positive ipaddress.is_global test. On Python 3.12.3 the denylist ACCEPTS 100.64.0.1 (is_private=False, is_reserved=False, is_global=False) - RFC6598 CGNAT / shared address space, routable to a carrier's or a cloud metadata-adjacent internal range. TEST-NET / benchmarking (198.18/15) / 240-4 are caught by is_reserved; CGNAT is the specific residual gap. runner.py is out of compliance with its own established I0003 standard.
findings.fix: Replace the denylist with the I0003 standard: reject unless ip_obj.is_global (i.e. `if not ip_obj.is_global: raise`). Keeps the same fail-safe intent while closing CGNAT and any future non-global range.
findings.repro_test: tests/test_runner_ssrf_listing_is_global.py::test_listing_guard_rejects_cgnat (TO WRITE in the serial fix-cut; RED on pristine 532 - the denylist accepts 100.64.0.1)
findings.source: Denylist read at runner.py:566-568; guarded sibling I0003 at provider_resolve_impl/_common.py; class = DP-11 / VR-P15.
findings.reachability_note: Config-driven subscription URL, operator-authenticated; the code's own docstring frames it as defense-in-depth hygiene ('an operator with write access could already shell to the box'). Second-order: listing-discovered <a href> URLs are re-enqueued WITHOUT re-passing even this guard (618 only checks startswith('http')), so a malicious listing page can seed the download path with off-host URLs - but the download path is unconstrained by design anyway (see runner_extractors ssrf=residual).
findings.witness: witnesses/run01_witnesses.py::W1 (re-derives the denylist predicate from live source and shows 100.64.0.1 accepted_but_not_global=True on Python 3.12.3; flips GREEN once the guard uses is_global)

findings.title: _build_ytdlp_cmd appends the URL with no '--' end-of-options separator -> a URL beginning with '-' is argument-injected into yt-dlp (--exec => RCE)
findings.detail: _build_ytdlp_cmd builds a list argv and does `cmd.append(url)` (102) with NO preceding `--` end-of-options marker; subprocess.run(cmd, shell=False) at 160. shell=False correctly blocks SHELL injection (an assurance), but yt-dlp's own CLI parser treats any argv element beginning with '-' as an OPTION, not a positional URL. Witnessed end-to-end: the real yt-dlp 2026.03.17 binary, handed the builder's output with url='--version', parsed the slot as the --version option (printed a version, exited 0, no fetch). yt-dlp exposes --exec (run an arbitrary command on the downloaded file) and --config-location (load a config that can itself contain --exec) -> a '-'-leading job URL is arbitrary command execution. This is a CONFIRMED real instance of the pilot's candidate pattern DP-CAP01-cand-1.
findings.fix: Insert an end-of-options separator immediately before the URL: `cmd.append('--'); cmd.append(url)` in _build_ytdlp_cmd. One line; makes a '-'-leading value un-parseable as an option regardless of caller.
findings.repro_test: tests/test_build_ytdlp_cmd_optsep.py::test_dashdash_before_url (TO WRITE in the serial fix-cut; RED on pristine 532 - no '--' precedes the url argv element)
findings.source: Builder at runner_extractors.py:83-103; sink at :160; reached from runner_challenge.py:49 (_try_ytdlp_fallback) with the job URL.
findings.reachability_note: Two gates: (1) config['use_ytdlp_fallback'] must be on (opt-in, default False, per-site); (2) the job URL must be able to begin with '-'. Some enqueue paths validate startswith('http') (app.py:1881, :4897) which blocks a '-'-leading URL, but MANY enqueue paths exist (api_bulk_enqueue, poll_sources [external plugin URLs], discover_all, saved_searches, capture_schedules) and several ingest EXTERNAL URLs; airtight non-reachability spans the APP/CORE_BD batches, so reachability is PROBABLE not confirmed (boundary-deferred, mirrors F-CAP01-01). The defect and its one-line fix stand regardless of current reachability.
findings.witness: witnesses/run01_witnesses.py::W2 (structural: no bare '--' before the url argv; behavioural: real yt-dlp 2026.03.17 parsed url='--version' as an option. SAFE probe - never --exec. Flips GREEN once '--' is inserted)

findings.title: float(config disk_threshold_gb / bandwidth_target_mbps) feeds a bounds compare with no math.isfinite guard (NaN evades the gate)
findings.detail: threshold=float(config.get('disk_threshold_gb',2.0)) (795) then `free < threshold` (799); target_mbps=float(config.get('bandwidth_target_mbps',0) or 0) (1058) then `target_mbps <= 0` (1059). Neither guards isfinite. A NaN in config makes `free < NaN` vacuously False -> the low_disk gate NEVER fires and the disk fills silently; +inf inverts it. Same class as I0004 (guarded in site_editor.py). Python's json.loads accepts a bare NaN token by default, so a hand-edited config.json can carry it.
findings.fix: Guard at the consuming site (defense-in-depth even if a validator exists upstream): `if not math.isfinite(threshold): threshold = <default>` before the compare, for both fields.
findings.repro_test: tests/test_runner_disk_threshold_isfinite.py::test_nan_threshold_still_fires_low_disk (TO WRITE in the serial fix-cut; RED on pristine 532)
findings.source: float() sites at runner.py:795,1058; guarded sibling I0004 at site_editor.py; class = DP-03 / VR-P08/P12.
findings.reachability_note: Operator-config fields; may be validated upstream by the I0004 site_editor/settings-center validator - whether THESE two fields flow through that validator (vs global_config direct load) is owned by the settings/site-editor batch. Filed low/probable pending that batch; the consuming code does not self-guard either way.
findings.witness: witnesses/run01_witnesses.py::W10 (both float() sites present with no isfinite; free<NaN evaluated False -> gate never fires)

false_positive_confirmations.triage_rule: an f-string inside self.log_event/print/sys.stderr.write is not a SQL sink even when the enclosing function is DB-adjacent (same rule as CAP-01 FP triage).

false_positive_confirmations.reason: the line is sys.stderr.write(f'  deep-detect: WARNING - resolve_providers=True for site {self.site_id!r}: ...') - a warning LOG; the only interpolation is a site id; no SQL.
false_positive_confirmations.triage_rule: sys.stderr.write f-string is a log sink, not a SQL sink.

false_positive_confirmations.reason: login_session is ASSIGNED on the line above via `login_session = getattr(self, '_manual_login_handle', None)` - getattr always returns (default None), so the name is always bound; there is no NameError path.
false_positive_confirmations.triage_rule: `x = getattr(obj, 'attr', None)` binds x unconditionally; a following `if x and hasattr(x, ...)` has no undefined-name risk.

new_invariants.statement: Every SSRF host classifier in the runner (currently _scrape_listing_urls) MUST use ipaddress.is_global as the positive allowlist test - not a denylist of is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_multicast/is_reserved/is_unspecified, which omits CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10. This is the runner-side twin of I0003.
new_invariants.promote_note: Promote to GUARDED when the serial fix-cut switches runner.py:566-568 to `not is_global` and adds a RED guard asserting 100.64.0.1 is rejected. Until then enforced only by this audit + witness W1.

new_invariants.statement: The yt-dlp fallback command builder MUST place a '--' end-of-options separator immediately before the URL argv element, so a URL beginning with '-' cannot be parsed by yt-dlp as an option (argument injection -> --exec RCE). List-form + shell=False is necessary but NOT sufficient.
new_invariants.promote_note: Promote to GUARDED when _build_ytdlp_cmd inserts '--' before the url and a RED guard asserts the built argv contains '--' immediately before a '-'-leading url. This is the concrete guard for DP-CAP01-cand-1.

new_patterns.rule: denylist-style SSRF IP classifier: flag any IP-safety gate that ORs is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_multicast/is_reserved/is_unspecified as its ACCEPT/REJECT test WITHOUT a positive ipaddress.is_global check. Denylists silently miss CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 (and any future non-global range). Strengthens DP-11 from 'no is_global' to 'enumerated-denylist-without-is_global'.
new_patterns.signature: ipaddress .is_private/.is_loopback/... OR-chain in a boolean guard with no .is_global in the same predicate

new_patterns.rule: [PROMOTE candidate->confirmed] list-form subprocess (shell=False) is NOT sufficient to clear a URL/path argv element: also require the value to be shape-validated so it cannot be read as an option (argument injection) - concretely, a '--' end-of-options separator before a request-derived URL argv.
new_patterns.signature: subprocess argv whose final element is a request-derived URL, with no '--' separator preceding it
new_patterns.confirmed_instance: F-RUN01-02 (runner_extractors.py:102/160) - FIRST confirmed real instance of the pilot candidate; promote in DEFECT_PATTERN_CATALOG.md at consolidation.
